title: Unintended continuous data collection
description: User may not be aware of the extent or duration of continuous sensor telemetry capture (heart rate, GPS, step counts) while wearing the device
assumptions: User assumes device is only for basic fitness tracking

title: Location tracking through GPS data
description: GPS position data collected by wearable device can be used to track user's movements and location history
assumptions: GPS is enabled and functioning

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Sensor telemetry data in transit from wearable device to processing system could be intercepted by unauthorized parties
assumptions: Data flows over network or wireless connection

title: Unintended data use by device
description: Wearable device may use collected sensor data for purposes beyond user's expectations (e.g., selling data, sharing with third parties)
assumptions: Device has access to collected data and may have third-party integrations

title: User identification through sensor data
description: Biometric and behavioral data (heart rate patterns, movement signatures) could be used to identify and profile the user
assumptions: Sensor data is unique to individual user

title: Excessive Personal Data Sharing at Source
description: Wearable device shares personal data (GPS traces, device ID, timestamps) that may not be strictly necessary for the intended exercise session tracking purpose, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: Assumes the wearable device is designed to share all sensor data without filtering based on necessity.

title: Data Flow Meta-Data Disclosure
description: Data in transit contains meta-data about the parties (P1 and P2) that could be used to link or identify them, potentially enabling tracking or profiling across devices.
assumptions: Assumes data flow metadata is not encrypted or anonymized.

title: Data Storage and Processing at Destination
description: Companion app receives and processes/stores personal data (exercise sessions, GPS traces, device ID, timestamps) which could lead to further disclosure or unauthorized access by third parties.
assumptions: Assumes the companion app may not have adequate access controls or data retention policies.

title: Data Interception During Transit
description: Personal data in transit between wearable device and companion app could be intercepted by third parties, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive health and location information.
assumptions: Assumes data may not be encrypted during transmission.

title: Data Storage Confidentiality at Destination
description: Companion app may not have adequate security measures to protect stored personal data, making it vulnerable to unauthorized access or data breaches.
assumptions: Assumes the companion app may not have proper encryption and access controls for stored data.

title: Data Integrity During Transit
description: Personal data in transit between wearable device and companion app could be tampered with, potentially altering exercise session data, GPS traces, or timestamps.
assumptions: Assumes data may not be integrity-protected during transmission.

title: Data Integrity at Destination
description: Companion app may not have adequate security measures to protect stored data from tampering, potentially altering exercise session data, GPS traces, or timestamps.
assumptions: Assumes the companion app may not have proper integrity controls for stored data.

title: Unawareness of data sharing implications
description: User may not be fully aware of the implications of sharing personal health data (calories, meals, weight) with the companion app, including potential secondary uses or data sharing with third parties.
assumptions: User is manually entering sensitive health data without full understanding of downstream processing.

title: Lack of control over data sharing
description: User may not have adequate control over how their personal health data is shared, processed, or used by the companion app beyond the intended purpose.
assumptions: User has limited ability to revoke or modify data sharing permissions after initial entry.

title: Data disclosure via metadata in transit
description: Meta-data about the parties (user and app) being used to link or identify them during data transmission could potentially be intercepted or observed.
assumptions: Data flows over network that may not be fully encrypted or monitored.

title: Data processing without user consent
description: The companion app may process the entered health data in ways that create privacy risks, such as profiling, sharing with third parties, or using for purposes beyond the user's expectations.
assumptions: App may have broad data processing capabilities not fully disclosed to the user.

title: Data Disclosure via Health Log Transfer
description: Health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) are transferred from the companion mobile app to the health log store, creating a data disclosure boundary. This transfer may expose personal health data to third parties or create unintended data sharing scenarios.
assumptions: The health log store may be accessible to third parties or may not have appropriate access controls.

title: Linkability through Data Flow
description: The data flow itself may create linkability between the companion app and health log store, potentially allowing correlation of health data with other data sources or user activities.
assumptions: The data flow metadata or patterns could be used to link the user's health data with other datasets.

title: Identification via Health Data Transfer
description: Health logs contain personal identifiers (weight, exercise patterns, calorie intake) that can be used to identify individuals, potentially enabling re-identification or profiling.
assumptions: The health log data contains or can be linked to personal identifiers.

title: Unintended Data Processing at Destination
description: The health log store may process health data in unintended ways, such as sharing with third parties, using for purposes beyond health tracking, or failing to implement appropriate security measures.
assumptions: The health log store may have broader access or processing capabilities than intended.

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: The companion mobile app may not comply with privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) when transferring health data to the health log store, potentially violating data minimization or consent requirements.
assumptions: The data transfer may not have proper legal basis or user consent.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The companion mobile app may collect and share more GPS location traces than strictly necessary for the intended functionality, violating the minimality principle for personal data collection.

title: Location Data in Transit Exposure
description: GPS location traces with timestamps are transmitted in transit between the app and location history store, potentially exposing location metadata that could be used to link or identify users.

title: Location Data Storage Without Adequate Access Controls
description: The location history store may not implement sufficient access controls to prevent unauthorized access to stored GPS location traces, leading to potential data disclosure to unauthorized parties.

title: Unnecessary Personal Data Disclosure
description: Health Log Store transfers calorie, weight, and exercise logs to Analytics Service for health-condition analysis. The data store may be disclosing more personal data than strictly required for the intended purpose, violating the minimality principle.

title: Data in Transit Exposure
description: Personal health data (calorie, weight, exercise logs) flows in transit between DataStore and Process. This data-centric threat involves potential interception or exposure of data while in transit, including metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them.

title: Data Processing and Storage Risks
description: Health Analytics Service receives and processes personal health data. The process may store, analyze, or share this data in ways that exceed the original intent, potentially leading to unintended disclosures or secondary uses of sensitive health information.

title: Profiling of individuals through inferred health insights
description: The analytics service infers health-condition risk indicators and trend flags that may reveal patterns about individuals' health status, potentially enabling profiling of individuals or groups based on their health data.
assumptions: The analytics service processes individual health data to generate insights that could be used to profile individuals or groups.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether the inferred insights are truly group-level or individual-level profiling.

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health data sharing
description: The analytics service may lack adequate cybersecurity measures when sharing sensitive health-related inferred insights with the companion app, creating privacy risks through inadequate risk management.
assumptions: Health analytics data requires proper cybersecurity risk management per privacy regulations.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about the specific cybersecurity controls in place at P3.

title: Inference of identity through data in transit
description: The data flow contains inferred health insights that could potentially be used to link or identify individuals if combined with other data sources or metadata about the parties involved.
assumptions: The inferred insights contain identifiable information that could be used to re-identify individuals.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether the inferred insights contain sufficient identifying information.

title: Linking via metadata in data flow
description: The data flow itself contains metadata that could be used to link the user's identity to their health condition indicators, potentially enabling profiling or tracking across different services.
assumptions: Assumes the flow metadata (e.g., timestamps, packet headers) could be intercepted and analyzed.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: Metadata analysis of mobile app data flows is not always possible in practice, but theoretically possible if traffic is captured.

title: Identification via health indicators in transit
description: The health condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) transmitted in the data flow could be used to identify the user's health status, potentially revealing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Assumes the data in transit is not properly encrypted or could be intercepted.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: Depends on encryption implementation and network security measures.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health information
description: The user (wearer) may disclose the displayed health condition indicators to third parties without consent, leading to potential privacy breaches and misuse of sensitive health data.
assumptions: Assumes the user may not be fully aware of the implications of sharing this information.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: User behavior varies; some users may be more cautious about sharing health information.

title: User unawareness of data usage implications
description: The user may not be fully aware of how their health data is being processed, stored, or shared beyond the app dashboard, leading to potential privacy risks.
assumptions: Assumes the user may not have read privacy policies or understand data handling practices.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: User awareness depends on privacy education and transparency in app design.

title: Non-compliance with health data protection regulations
description: The display of sensitive health indicators to the user may not comply with applicable health data protection regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR), leading to legal and organizational risk.
assumptions: Assumes the app may not have proper compliance measures for health data handling.
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty: Specific regulatory requirements vary by jurisdiction and may not be fully covered in the current analysis.

title: Explicit disclosure of personal health data to third-party cloud provider
description: The Health Analytics Service explicitly transfers full health and location datasets to the Cloud Hosting Provider (EE2), constituting an intentional disclosure of personal data to a known third party. This violates the minimality principle as the full dataset may contain more personal data than strictly required for the intended purpose.
assumptions: The transfer is intentional and by design for hosting and replication purposes.

title: Data in transit disclosure via metadata
description: Data in transit between P3 and EE2 may contain metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them, including information about the nature of the data being transferred, which could be used to infer sensitive information about the health analytics service and its users.
assumptions: Metadata can be extracted from data flows during transmission.

title: Implicit disclosure through data replication
description: The Cloud Hosting Provider replicates the health and location datasets, which may result in implicit disclosure of personal data to multiple locations or entities, potentially violating data sovereignty and jurisdictional requirements.
assumptions: Cloud providers typically replicate data across multiple regions for redundancy and performance.

title: Data sovereignty and jurisdictional concerns
description: The Health Analytics Service transfers personal data to a third-party cloud provider, which may be located in a different jurisdiction. This raises concerns about compliance with local data protection laws and the ability to control where personal data is stored and processed.
assumptions: The Cloud Hosting Provider operates in a jurisdiction with different data protection requirements than the originating organization.

title: Information leakage through analytics data
description: The Cloud Hosting Provider may process or analyze the analytics data and models, potentially leading to unintended information leakage about the health analytics service's operations, algorithms, or business logic.
assumptions: The Cloud Hosting Provider may have access to the analytics data and models for hosting purposes.
